SHANGHAI, 1st May 1935.

Sir,

With reference to your letter of 4 April 1935,
D.4408, for which I wish to express my sincere thanks,
it may be of interest to you that, according to infor-
mation received, Mrs.Reimer's daughter is earning a
small salary in Holland and receives financial assistance
from her father, who however is not prepared to support
his former wife. As it was feared that Mrs.Reimer would
become a charge to the community, a visé for travelling
to Holland was refused.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

No. ____
Date April 4, 19 33.

Subject (in full) Further report regarding Mrs. M.W. Reimer subject of
enquiries from Netherlands Consulate General.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by [签名]

Further enquiries regarding Mrs. M.W. Reimer show that
she is from Ekaterinoslav Province, South Russia, "Menonite"
extraction. Her former husband Peter Henrich Reimer is from
Tauris Province, Krimea also "Menonite" extraction. Before
the Great War the "Menonite" colonists as they then called
themselves were known among the Russian population as German
(Nemzi). During the Great War the Russian Government issued
orders that persons residing in certain parts of the German
colonists region were to be sent to Siberia etc. A number of
"Menonites" then declared that they originated from Netherlands
and Denmark, and that the German colonists environment during
generations had resulted the "Menonite" in adoption of the
Plat. - German dialect. Some "Menonites" produced documents
proving this claim. The family of Mrs. Reimer and of her
husband likewise claimed their originated from the Netherlands.

Mrs. Reimer registered herself with King's
Daughter's Society in Shanghai as a Russian, of Netherlands
origin. She is not in possession of any documents to prove
this claim. She usually associates with Germans and is known
to have obtained support from local German friends.

[签名]
D. S.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

编号 ____
日期 1933年4月4日。

主题（全称） 关于荷兰总领事馆查询对象 M.W. 赖默夫人的进一步报告。

由 D.S. Tcheremshansky 撰写。由 [签名] 转呈

对 M.W. 赖默夫人的进一步调查显示，她来自南俄罗斯叶卡捷琳诺斯拉夫省（Ekaterinoslav Province），系“门诺派”（Menonite）后裔。她的前夫彼得·亨里希·赖默（Peter Henrich Reimer）来自克里米亚陶里斯省（Tauris Province, Krimea），亦为“门诺派”后裔。在大战之前，“门诺派”殖民者（他们当时如此自称）在俄罗斯人口中被称为德国人（Nemzi）。大战期间，俄罗斯政府发布命令，将居住在德国殖民者地区某些部分的人送往西伯利亚等地。随后，一些“门诺派”人士宣称他们源自荷兰和丹麦，并称几代人的德国殖民者环境导致“门诺派”采用了低地德语方言。一些“门诺派”人士出具了证明这一主张的文件。赖默夫人及其丈夫的家族同样声称他们源自荷兰。

赖默夫人在上海的“国王女儿会”（King's Daughter's Society）注册时，登记为具有荷兰血统的俄罗斯人。她没有任何文件可以证明这一主张。她通常与德国人来往，并已知从当地德国朋友处获得资助。

[签名]
D. S.

特别股主管。

C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 4408
Date 3 / 4 / 33

SHANGHAI, 28th March 1933.

Sir,

I have the honour to refer to our correspondence con-
cerning Mrs. M. W. Reimer (your letter D. 4408, d. d. 2 Febr.
1933, my letter No. 354 d. d. 3 Febr. 1933) and to inform
you that I am now in receipt of a telegram from the Ministry
of Foreign Affairs at The Hague to the effect that Mrs.
Reimer's application for entry into The Netherlands has been
refused. So far I am unaware of the reasons for this de-
cision, but in any case it would be interesting to know, in
case this point has been cleared up, whether Mr. Reimer is of
Netherlands or of German extraction.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

〔签名〕
Chinese Secretary.

T. P. Givans, Esquire,
Officer i/c Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.

No. 354.

SHANGHAI, 3 February 1933 .

Sir,

With reference to the detective report, kindly for-
warded by your letter of 2 February 1933, concerning Mrs.
Reimer, I wish to draw your kind attention to the fact that,
(1) contrary to the usage established by the Shanghai Municipal
Council, the word "Dutch" is used twice for "Netherlands".
In connection with the statement according to which
Mr. Reimer is of Netherlands or German extraction, it would
(2) be of interest to know which. The Netherlands equivalents
of his Christian names would be : Pieter Hendrik, but a
Russian or German environment may have brought about cor-
ruptions of spelling, also in the family name.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

〔此处为手写签名〕
Chinese Secretary.

T. P. Givens, Esquire,
Officer i/c Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

and make further
inquiries re No. 2 and
report.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch S.S.
REPORT
Date February 1, 1933.

Subject (in full) Mrs. M.W. Reimer, subject to the enquiry from
the Netherlands Consulate-General.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the letter of January 10, 1933
from the Netherlands Consulate-General regarding Mrs. Maria
Wilhelmovna (Vassilieva) Reimer, her identity and records
as known to the Municipal Police are as follows :
Mrs. Reimer is a Russian of Dutch extraction,
native of Ekaterinoslav Province, born on December 19, 1880.
She arrived in China from Russia when about 12 years of ago.
She first registered in Shanghai with the Russian Emigrants
Committee on February 1923. While in Russia she was separated
from her husband one Peter Henrich Reimer, Russian of Dutch
or German extraction, Menonite by religion, born 1874 at
Tavris Province. This marriage resulted in a family of a
daughter Maria, now aged about 24 years and two sons, one
residing at Chicago, U.S.A. and another in Canada. Her
husband who resided in Shanghai from 1924 was a representative
of "International Harvester Co.", 4-8 Yuen Ming Yuen Road.
This firm is connected with the well known local form "Andersen,
Meyer & Co." In 1929 he left for Europe accompanied by his
daughter Maria Reimer.
Mrs. Reimer declared in her statement to the King's
Daughter's Society that she failed to gain any information of
her husband for some years and then finally found him in
Tsingtae (during 1923-1925) married again. Her marriage was
then dissolved and she received some $5.000 as settlement.
She then left for Harbin where she met a Russian whom she
married (?) but he later left her taking with him all her money.
The whereabouts of this second husband is at present unknown
to her. Mrs. Reimer arrived in Shanghai on February 25, 1932
and since this time was employed at the various places as a

主题（全称） M.W. 赖默夫人，荷兰总领事馆查询对象。

由 D.S. Tcheremshansky 撰写。由 [签名] 转呈

关于荷兰总领事馆1933年1月10日就玛丽亚·威廉莫夫娜（瓦西里耶娃）赖默（Maria Wilhelmovna (Vassilieva) Reimer）夫人一事去信，工部局警务处所知的其身份及记录如下：
赖默夫人是具有荷兰血统的俄罗斯人，原籍叶卡捷琳诺斯拉夫省，生于1880年12月19日。她约在12年前从俄罗斯抵达中国。她于1923年2月首次在上海俄罗斯移民委员会注册。在俄罗斯期间，她与丈夫彼得·亨里希·赖默分居，后者是具有荷兰或德国血统的俄罗斯人，门诺派教徒，1874年生于陶里斯省（Tavris Province）。这段婚姻育有一女玛丽亚，现年约24岁，以及两子，一子居住在美国芝加哥，另一子在加拿大。其丈夫自1924年起居住在上海，是“国际收割机公司”（International Harvester Co.）的代表，地址为圆明园路4-8号。该公司与当地知名的“安得生、美尔洋行”（Andersen, Meyer & Co.）有关联。1929年，他携女儿玛丽亚·赖默前往欧洲。
赖默夫人在向“国王女儿会”提交的声明中称，她多年未能获得丈夫的任何消息，后来终于在青岛（1923-1925年间）发现他已再婚。随后她的婚姻解除，并获得约5,000美元作为安置费。之后她前往哈尔滨，在那里遇到一名俄罗斯人并与之结婚（？），但后来该男子离开她时带走了她所有的钱。目前她不知道这第二任丈夫的下落。赖默夫人于1932年2月25日抵达上海，此后曾在各处受雇担任

or other similar organizations. It is stated that during the

CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.

No. 104

CONFIDENTIEEL

SHANGHAI, 10 January 1933.

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that I received an application for a visa for the Netherlands from Mrs. M.W. Reimer, a housekeeper by profession, born in Yekaterinoslav on 19 December 1880, at present staying in the Municipal Sanitorium on Hungjao Road.

She has a passport issued by the Bureau of Public Safety at Shanghai on 27 Februari 1932, No. 849 and is registered there under 7692/32.

She stated that she arrived in China from Vladivostok about 12 years ago, staying in Tsingtao for about 3½ years, coming afterwards to Shanghai, where she had employments at various places, a.o. at the King's Daughters' Convalescent Home. She was divorced from her husband, who is at present living in The Hague, and desires to join her daughter, Maria Petrovna Reimer, who left China with her father at the end of 1929, and who is also staying in the Netherlands now. The daughter appears to have a position as a bookkeeper in Rotterdam and it is the intention of the applicant, who apparently is in bad health, to join her there.

Her son is said to have gone to Canada.

I would be much obliged to know whether anything is known against the applicant from a political or moral point of view. Meanwhile this Consulate will try to find out whether Mrs. Reimer's daughter wishes to receive her mother, so that, should a visa be granted, (which I intend not to do without consulting the authorities at home) she will not be a charge to the community.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

〔此处为签名及印章，难以辨认〕

F. P. Givens, Esquire,
Officer i/c Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

（右上角手写批注：SPECIAL MUNI POLICE / C.I.D. REGISTRY / No. D 11408 / Date 12/1/33）
（左侧手写批注：$2, / For attention / Please Jfy）

荷兰驻华中总领事馆
电话 AD. HOLLANDIA。

第 104 号

机密

上海，1933年1月10日。

先生：

谨通知您，我收到 M.W. 赖默夫人的荷兰签证申请。赖默夫人职业为管家，1880年12月19日生于叶卡捷琳诺斯拉夫，目前住在虹桥路市立疗养院。

她持有上海公安局于1932年2月27日签发的护照，编号849，并在该局注册号为7692/32。

她称约12年前从符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）抵达中国，在青岛停留约3年半，随后来到上海，曾在多处就业，其中包括在“国王女儿康复之家”（King's Daughters' Convalescent Home）。她已与丈夫离婚，其丈夫目前居住在海牙，她希望与其女儿玛丽亚·彼得罗夫娜·赖默（Maria Petrovna Reimer）团聚。她的女儿于1929年底随父亲离开中国，目前也居住在荷兰。女儿似乎在鹿特丹有一份簿记员的工作，申请人显然健康状况不佳，打算前往那里与女儿团聚。

据说她的儿子已前往加拿大。

若能从政治或道德角度得知是否有任何针对申请人的不良记录，我将不胜感激。同时，本领事馆将尝试查明赖默夫人的女儿是否愿意接收其母亲，以便如果签发签证（我打算在未咨询国内当局之前不予签发），她不会成为社会负担。

此致
敬礼

〔此处为签名及印章，难以辨认〕

F. P. Givens 先生，
特别股主管，
上海公共租界工部局警务处，
上海。

（右上角手写批注：特别工部局警务处 / 刑事侦缉处登记处 / 编号 D 11408 / 日期 1933年1月12日）
